newsitem.title: CHINA: Hainan orders unlisted companies to post results.
newsitem.headline: Hainan orders unlisted companies to post results.

text.p: Securities authorities in China's southern Hainan province have threatened to punish unlisted shareholding companies that disobey a rule that they post annual results, China Securities News said on Monday.

The rule, introduced in early 1996, made Hainan, an island in the South China Sea, the first Chinese province to force unlisted companies to release results in the same manner as listed companies, the newspaper said.
In 1996, 36 unlisted companies that failed to release annual results were fined 10,000 yuan ($1,205) each, it said.
The order, which would be welcomed by shareholders, would help companies standardise their operations, it added. It gave no further details.
